correctness.rationale: Exact orthogonal two-row Hadamard coupling takes all signed one-hot states bijectively to independent dense sign pairs. Independent hashes/signs across blocks and columns give the full dense-entry law. Conversely rank collapse of two unit columns requires every block to collide and share sign, probability 2^(1-s)/product b_j, versus 2^(1-m) for dense signs, with equality iff b_j<=2 because b_j<=2^(b_j-1). This proves necessity, sufficiency and sharp sparsity bound s>=ceil(m/2) for all m,n>=2.

value.rationale: Full equality of every fixed-input Gram-derived statistic is a useful sharp structural property of sparse sketches, beyond a concentration estimate. The iff block-width classification and attained minimum nonzero count identify precisely how far sparsity can be reduced while retaining the entire dense-sign Gram law. No speedup or floating-point performance is inferred.
